title: F108--620-26-206 Asbestos Abatement
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 2, intends to issue Solicitation 36C24227R0010 for Project 620-26-206 Asbestos Abatement at Montrose VA Medical Center, 2094 Albany Post Rd, Montrose, NY 10548. This notice is for pre-solicitation purposes only and is issued to provide advance notice of the Government's intent to solicit this construction requirement. This notice is not a request for quotes, proposals, or bids, and no contract award will be made as a result of this announcement. The official solicitation is anticipated to be posted on or about November 6, 2026, on SAM.gov, at which time all solicitation documents, including the Statement of Work, drawings, specifications, and proposal submission instructions, will be made available. This procurement is anticipated to be issued as a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. Eligible SDVOSBs are encouraged to submit an offer upon release of the solicitation. All prospective offerors must be currently registered in www.sam.gov, www.dnb.com (Duns and Bradstreet) and be registered and verified as a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) in https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ at the time of offer submission and before award of this procurement. The applicable NAICS Code is 562910 with a small business size standard of $25.0 million. The Magnitude of Construction for this project is between $100,000 and $250,000. Scope of Work: The Montrose VA Medical Center anticipates awarding a construction contract for asbestos abatement in the Building 3 Physical Therapy/Sleep Study area. The project involves asbestos abatement within an approximately 2,300-square-foot area, including approximately 100 square feet of radiator heat shielding. Work includes the removal and proper disposal of friable and non-friable asbestos-containing materials (ACM), associated demolition, utility modifications, and site restoration as required by the contract drawings and specifications. The Contractor shall furnish all necessary labor, materials, equipment, supervision, and services to complete the work in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations, including VA safety and infection-control requirements and New York State asbestos-abatement regulations. Work may require evening or weekend operations to minimize disruption to facility occupants. Period of Performance: The period of performance for Abatement shall be 365 days from Notice to Proceed (NTP). All other details and information shall be contained in the solicitation which shall be posted on www.sam.gov. The response submittal address, date and time will be included in the solicitation

title: C1DA--657-27-209JB Renovate Main Lobby, Bldgs 1 & 53
description: Modification 2 to Presolicitation Notice 36C25527R0007, P/N 657-27-209JB, Project Title: Renovate Building 1 and 53 Main Lobbies. This modification provides answers to RFIs received, revised evaluation criteria and revised supplement B per below RFIs. The SF330 submission due date is extended from November 10, 2026 to November 16, 2026. RFIs Received with VA Responses in blue text: Construction Budget questions: Is that the Estimated Cost of Construction or the maximum for the A/E Design Fee? Estimated Cost of Construction If the $949,026 is the construction budget, this appears low in today's environment given that over 6,000 SF needs to be renovated. Can the VA please re-evaluate this budget and provide an update? The construction budget that was originally used in the supplement B pre-solicitation notice is incorrect. A revised supplement B is attached, changing the construction cost estimate from $949,026 to $725,873. The Construction budget is set and cannot be changed until the design process is underway. Key Personnel questions: The Presolicitation Notice lists: Supervisory, Fire Protection Engineer, Certified Professional Industrial Hygienist, and Life Safety Engineer. The Statement of Work and Supplement B list: Communications (voice/data), Interior Design, VPIH, Plumbing (including fire protection), and a 3rd Party Fire Protection Review. Questions: Which positions require resumes in Section E? What is the intended role of "Supervisory"? Per the SOW & Supplement B the following positions require resumes: Project Manager, Architectural, Mechanical, Electrical, Communication (voice data) Plumbing (Including Fire Protection), Structural, Interior Design, VPIH, Cost Estimator and a 3rd Party Fire Protection Review. Project manager is Supervisory Industrial Hygienist/Asbeston Project Designer: Question: Is an ABIH Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) acceptable for this position, and does a CIH satisfy the requirement for the VPIH and the state-accredited Asbestos Project Designer? If these must be separate individuals, should both be identified in the SF330? A CIH satisfies the requirement for the VPIH and the state-accredited Asbestos Project Designer. They can be the same individual. Site Visit: Supplement B, page 6, Section III.6.g: the A/E "shall meet with the COR at the proposed project site" prior to submitting a response Presolicitation Notice, page 4: "Personal visits to discuss this announcement will not be allowed" and only "the most highly rated firm must physically come to the site" before pricing Question: Please confirm that no site visit is required before the SF330 submission. No site visit is required prior to SF330 submission. Laboratory and Special Room Rquirements: Presolicitation Notice, page 7, Evaluation Criteria 2, Specialized Experience and Technical Competence: "laboratory requirements for the firm" Supplement B, page 18, Section B6.II.1: "floor plans of special rooms such as the endoscopy suite, recovery room, etc." Questions: Neither a laboratory nor an endoscopy suite or recovery room appears in the project scope. Do any of these requirements apply to this project? These requirements do not apply to this project. Can the VA please release updated and corrected documents? The evaluation criteria 2 will be changed to remove laboratory requirements for the firm and the COR will revise Supplement B to remove the endoscopy suite and recovery room from the Supplement B.

title: 66--IRA - High-Temperature Chamber Furnace
description: IRA High-Temperature Chamber Furnace The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), National Energy Technology Laboratory (NETL), is conducting market research to identify contractors capable of providing a high-temperature chamber furnace for the processing of carbon materials at temperatures up to 2600 �C. The required specifications of this High-Temperature Chamber Furnace are outlined in Attachment A to this Sources Sought. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE that is open to all companies and is for information and planning purposes and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government. This Sources Sought Notice is released pursuant to FAR Part 10 Market Research and is issued for the purpose of identifying available sources (interested entities) capable of performing the requirement. This is not a solicitation announcement for proposals and NO CONTRACT will be awarded from this announcement. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement or any follow-up information requests. The information gathered from this Sources Sought Notice will be utilized in the Government's determination for the business type utilized in the RFQ. PURPOSE: The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to solicit input and gauge interest among those parties capable of providing a High-Temperature Chamber Furnace for the processing of carbon materials at temperatures up to 2600 �C in accordance with the specifications outlined in Attachment A to this Source Sought. DESCRIPTION: The National Energy Technology Laboratory (NETL) is part of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratory system and is owned and operated by the DOE. NETL supports the DOE mission to advance the energy security of the United States. As part of this of this mission, NETL has a need for a high-temperature chamber furnace for the processing of carbon materials at temperatures up to 2600 �C. The information being solicited includes, but is not limited to, the following: 1. A cover page (no longer than one page) which provides the following information: The entities name, address, phone number, email address for the point of contact, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number, CAGE code (if applicable), and business size. Specify the small business classification: small business, small-disadvantaged business, woman owned, veteran owned, disabled veteran owned, 8(a) or HUB Zone. The cover page should also include the country in which the furnace would be manufactured in. 2. A brief Statement of Capabilities detailing how your company meets the requirements outlined in Attachment A � Technical Specifications. For consistency purposes, responses are to be submitted electronically in either MS Word (.doc or .docx) or Adobe Acrobat (.pdf) format using a minimum of 11-point font and allowing for 1-inch margins no more than 20 pages in length, inclusive of the cover page. Information regarding how to submit information via FedConnect can be found at https://www.fedconnect.net. You are strongly encouraged to submit your Capability Statement in response to this Sources Sought Notice at least 24 hours before the specified due date in order to have time to resolve any transmission problems. Reminder, the Solicitation and Amendments must be signed and included with the proposal submission. 12 August Amendment 02 to revise documents as a result of Q&A. 28 Jul 26 Amendment 01 to revised documents as a result of Q&A. 10 Jul 26 Center Console Refresh addresses critical obsolescence issues within the KC-135 Refueling Tanker aircraft. The US Air Force needs an updated Fuel System (FS), Flight Display System (FDS), and Flight Computer due to obsolescence and is looking for innovative ideas to not only replace but improve these systems with turn-key solutions enabling supportability and future growth. The FS, FDS, Flight Computer, and the future growth/adaptability define the scope of the CCR program. The program scope also includes the addition of autothrottle systems. The anticipated contract will be a Cost-Plus Incentive Fee (CPIF) for EMD, Firm Fixed Price (FFP) for Production and Deployment (P&D), single award indefinite delivery/quantity type contract comprised of One (1) 48-month Base Period with Six (6) 1-Year Option Periods and a projected period of performance from July 2028 to June 2038. title: Industry Day Announcement Supply Chain Illumination
description: Industry Day Announcement Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Armament Directorate Supply Chain Illumination Capability Hosted by AFLCMC/EB BLUF: AFLCMC/EB requires a secure, scalable, AI-assisted federated data capability that integrates but not unnecessarily replaces existing government, Service, and contractor data sources. The capability must provide end-to-end supply-chain mapping, risk identification and assessment, near-real-time situational awareness, mitigation tracking, and evidence-based decision support for priority munition programs, initially within the Long-Range Weapons, Affordable Munition, and Adaptive Weapons portfolios, with potential expansion across the Armament Directorate portfolio. 1. Introduction The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Armament Directorate (EB), plans to conduct a virtual Industry Day to conduct market research and obtain industry feedback regarding a potential Supply Chain Illumination capability for the munitions enterprise. The Armament Directorate is pursuing an artificial intelligence-assisted, federated data capability to map critical munition supply chains to raw-material sources. The intended capability would provide enterprise-level visibility into supply-chain dependencies, bottlenecks, supplier risks, competing demands, and mitigation actions in support of senior-leader decision-making and mission outcomes. This Industry Day is intended to inform the Government�s market research under Federal Acquisition Regulation Part 10 and help identify mature, scalable commercial and non-traditional solutions that can support the Directorate�s supply-chain visibility requirements. This announcement does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), solicitation, commitment, or promise to issue a solicitation in the future. 2. Background The Armament Directorate currently lacks an integrated mechanism to assess critical supply-chain risk across its acquisition divisions, military Services, and contractor-supported weapon systems. Existing data sources are fragmented (data lives in siloed systems), contractor logistics support arrangements can limit visibility into multi-tier supply chains, and shared dependencies across military and commercial demand can create unanticipated production risk. The Government seeks to improve end-to-end visibility of materials, suppliers, production dependencies, single points of failure, foreign-source dependencies, and mitigation actions across priority munition portfolios down to the raw materials at the lowest of sub-tier suppliers. The initial proof of concept is expected to focus on PAE-prioritized programs within the Long-Range Weapons, Affordable Munition, and Adaptive Weapons portfolios, with potential expansion across the Armament Directorate weapon-system portfolio. 3. Industry Day Objectives The Government seeks industry feedback on approaches to establish a secure, scalable Supply Chain Illumination capability that can: Map supply chains from end item to raw-material origin for critical munition programs, through all tiers of subcontractors. Federate existing government, Service, and contractor data sources without unnecessarily replacing established systems. Identify and assess supply-chain risks, including bottlenecks, single points of failure, constrained materials, supplier financial and manufacturing risk, foreign influence, and competing demands. Support data-sharing standards and interfaces that protect legitimate competition sensitive information while providing the Government sufficient visibility for risk management and decision support. Enable near-real-time situational awareness through application programming interfaces and other appropriate data-exchange mechanisms. Apply AI-assisted analytics, including machine-learning and knowledge-graph approaches, to identify relationships, risks, and mitigation options across complex, multi-tier supply chains. Track mitigation actions through end-item delivery and produce evidence suitable for waiver assessments and senior-leader decision-making. Integrate with relevant enterprise architectures and platforms, including existing Air Force, Army, Navy, and digital Bill of Materials efforts, as appropriate. 4. Event Details for the Virtual Industry Day Open to All Contractors Date: 15 December 2026 Time: 0900hrs CST Location/Platform: Teams Link Classification: Unclassified Registration Deadline: 16 November 2026 The Government will provide an overview of the operational problem, desired endstate, preliminary technical considerations, and potential next steps. The agenda may also include question-and-answer sessions and opportunities for industry participants to provide oral or written feedback. 5. Registration and Participation Registration is required. Interested organizations should submit the following information no later than 16 November 2026: Company name Company address Attendee name, title, email address, and telephone number Identification of the company�s primary point of contact A brief description of the company�s relevant capability or experience Any requested accessibility or administrative support requirements Submit registration information to: AFLCMC EB, Bryant Callahan (850) 882-0260, bryant.callahan.3@us.af.mil. 6. Follow-On Engagement Following Industry Day, the Government may issue a Request for Information, schedule one-on-one market-research discussions, request white papers, or conduct other market-research activities for live demonstrated capabilities only. Participation in Industry Day is not required for participation in any future acquisition or market-research activity unless expressly stated in a future notice. 7. Individual Demonstration Sessions Although not required, contractors may request one-on-one discussions for the sole purpose of providing a live demonstration that addresses the following questions for munitions: Supply Chain Risk: Which suppliers, components, and lower-tier dependencies present the greatest risk to weapon system readiness and production schedules? Operational Performance: How do suppliers lead times, material availability, and supply chain disruptions influence production delays and repair turnaround times? Investment Prioritization: Which supply chain vulnerabilities should receive priority investment to improve production capacity, reduce delays, and strengthen operational readiness? Predictive Analytics: To what extent can historical supplier performance, component lead times, and material shortages predict future supply chain disruptions? To coordinate a one-on-one session with the Government, contract Bryant Callahan, as shown in paragraph 9. Any one-on-one session will be scheduled after the Virtual Industry Day on15 December 2026. 8. Informational Notice THIS IS AN INFORMATIVE POSTING. This announcement is issued solely for planning and market research purposes. It does not constitute RFP, solicitation, contract, or commitment by the Government to procure any supply or service. The Government is not requesting proposals currently. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting registration materials, participating in Industry Day, providing feedback, or responding to any subsequent market research request. This language follows the informative-posting framework used in the supplied Industry Day announcement. 9. Point of Contact Primary Point of Contact: Bryant Callahan AFLCMC/EB bryant.callahan.3@us.af.mil 850-797-4770 Contracting Point of Contact: Patricia Chisholm patricia.chisholm@us.af.mil 850-882-6935

description: The Department of the Navy, Naval Surface Warfare Center, Carderock Division (NSWCCD), is soliciting services ranging from advancements in software standards and technologies for data processing, storage, simulation/generation, and visualization to the development of new software capabilities for Navy systems afloat and ashore.The Government is soliciting this requirement as a total small-business set-aside. title: SB ERS MATOC, USACE Northwestern Division and EPA Region 2
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Kansas City District is procuring a Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for Environmental Remediation Services (ERS) in support of United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Northwestern Division (NWD) and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Region 2. The MATOC will be procured on a competitive basis as a total small business (SB) set-aside under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 562910 Environmental Remediation Services. The scope of the SB ERS MATOC includes in-situ thermal remediation, in-situ chemical oxidation, and other chemical stabilization of contamination; operations and maintenance of remediation systems including large scale groundwater treatment plants, soil vapor extraction systems, and air sparge systems; preparation of work plans; studies with associated reports; multiple phases of field investigations; preliminary assessments; site inspections and remedial site inspections; remedial investigations; feasibility studies; Engineering Evaluation Cost Analysis; monitoring well installation and sampling; short and long term monitoring/long term operations or Long Term Response Action (LTRA); data management; data interpretation; engineering evaluation and corrective actions; optimization studies; ground-water modeling; geophysical surveys; remediation cost estimates; management of non-hazardous and hazardous investigative derived waste; environmental and human health risk assessments; risk based remediation; air emission issues including vapor intrusion; surface water discharge; applying for environmental permits; remedial design; well abandonment; meetings; public meeting participation; preparation of presentation material both written and visual; hydrological, sediment and soil studies; project reports; engineering support and/or design; value engineering studies; operations and maintenance for hazardous, toxic, and radioactive waste (HTRW) sites; energy evaluations for remediation systems; remedial action plans; remedial actions; removal action plans; removal actions; construction support; site closeout/decision documents; abandoned mines program support; and future project programming and scheduling support. The solicitation will be made available no earlier than 15 days after this presolicitation notice. All responsible sources may submit a proposal in response to the solicitation, which the government will consider in the award decision. This notice does not constitute a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor to pay for any costs incurred as a result in replying to this notice. This notice should not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose.

PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. title: Draft Solicitation - Aberdeen Test Center Welding, Machining, Painting, and Fabrication Services
description: This Combined Synopsis/Solicitation, Solicitation Number W91CRB-27-R-A002, is issued by the Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG) for commercial services. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 333992 (Welding and Soldering Equipment Manufacturing) with a small business size standard of 1,250 employees. This acquisition is a 100 percent Small Business Set-Aside under Product Service Code (PSC) K034. The resulting contract will be a single-award hybrid Time-and-Materials (T&M) and Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with a minimum guarantee of $100.00. Place of performance is the U.S. Army Aberdeen Test Center (ATC), Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland. The ordering period is 9 December 2026 through 8 December 2031, inclusive of a 45-day transition period. Source selection will be conducted using the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) process evaluating Technical, Past Performance, and Price factors on an Acceptable/Unacceptable basis. This requirement is for non-personal commercial services to provide welding, machining, painting, and fabrication support to the ATC Welding Fabrication, Machining, and Paint Shops. The contractor shall furnish the personnel, management, supervision, and resources (except Government-Furnished Property) necessary to support the Automotive, Command Staff, Live Fire, Virtual Test & Electronics, and Warfighter cores on a performance-based basis. Full technical requirements, labor category qualifications, Level of Effort estimates, Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan, Government-Furnished Property listing, and Contract Data Requirements Lists are contained in the attached solicitation package and are incorporated by reference. The posting and issue date of this Combined Synopsis/Solicitation is 2 November 2026. Questions are due no later than 9 September 2026 at 3:00 PM Eastern Standard Time. Proposals are due no later than 2:00 PM Eastern Time on 16 November 2026. Proposals shall remain valid for a period of at least 180 days from the closing date. Proposals must be submitted electronically to both Noah Lane, Contract Specialist, at noah.r.lane.civ@army.mil and Todd M. Strasavich, Contracting Officer, at todd.m.strasavich.civ@army.mil. Late proposals may not be considered. Offerors shall submit four volumes (Technical limited to 25 pages, Past Performance limited to 15 pages, Price, and Certifications/Representations). Complete submission instructions are provided in the attached solicitation package. The full solicitation package, consisting of the Performance Work Statement, Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan, Government-Furnished Property Listing, Labor Categories and Qualifications, Level of Effort Spreadsheet, and CDRL Exhibits AA through AC, is attached and incorporated by reference. Questions shall be submitted in writing to the points of contact identified above. Any amendments will be posted to SAM.gov. Offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for amendments.

See attached documents titled: �Requirements � 70Z03827QB0000010,� �Terms and Conditions � 70Z03827QB0000010� and �Redacted J and A � 70Z03827QB0000010�. 52.217-6 Option for Increased Quantity (MAR 1989) applies to this acquisition and is tailored as follows: The Government may increase the quantity of supplies called for in the Schedule, for Line Item 1 by up to a quantity of Twenty (20), at the unit price specified, up to a maximum quantity of Thirty (30). Delivery of the added items shall continue at the same rate as the like items call for under the Purchase Order, unless the parties otherwise agree. ***Please note that if the USCG chooses to exercise any optional quantity modification, such modifications will be issued unilaterally to the contractor. description: The Government intends to conduct this aquisition through a two-phased technical submission with an advisory down-select. Title: National Performance Management Research Data Set (NPMRDS) Technical and Data-Sharing Support Solicitation Release Date: Thursday, November 12, 2026 (11/12/2026) Technical Questions (Q&A) Due: 2:00 PM Eastern Time (ET) Monday, November 16, 2026 (11/16/2026) Phase 1 Technical Submission Due : 2:00 PM Eastern Time (ET) Monday, November 16, 2026 (11/16/2026) Phase 2 Technical Submission and Price Quotation Due: 2:00 PM Eastern Time (ET) Monday, November 30, 2026 (11/30/2026) PLEASE NOTE: Please read the attached RFQ carefully and thoroughly. All technical submissions, price quotations, and questions must be submitted electronically via email in accordance with the RFQ instructions. Please do not upload or submit any technical submissions, price quotations, or questions to SAM.gov. Any technical submissions, price quotations, or questions submitted via SAM.gov will not be considered. Backround: FHWA is an agency within the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) with a mission to improve safety and mobility on our nation�s highways through national leadership, innovation, and program delivery. With continued growth in both traffic and freight volumes, significant portions of the transportation system experience congested conditions on a regular basis, leading to unreliable service to the American people. FHWA has engaged in broad activities in partnership with State and local transportation agencies to improve travel reliability and mitigate congestion. From a traffic flow standpoint, these activities include but are not limited to: Real-time and forecasted information; Measuring/monitoring passenger and freight system performance; Analytical foundation/tools/data; State of the art technologies and strategies, including operational tests of intelligent transportation system (ITS) technologies; Development of standards for information exchange; Guidance and funding for infrastructure and ITS projects; Integration across system elements, jurisdictions, and modes; and Assistance for transportation and planning professionals in developing the knowledge and skills needed to do their jobs effectively. The objective of the requirement is to gain access to timely and quality travel time data, referred to as NPMRDS data, covering the National Highway System (NHS) and obtain technical support needed by Federal, State, and local agencies to carry out data application and data analysis related to Transportation Performance Management (TPM).

Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

Bill Young Veterans Medical Center Surgery Service located at 10000 Bay Pines Blvd. Bay Pines, Fl. 33744 is seeking procurement of six transducers and six trays from GE Healthcare. The department requires replacement of ultrasound transducers that have reached the end of their operational life and can no longer be repaired or supported by the manufacturer. 2. Background: These transducers are vital to patient diagnostic and procedural imaging. The existing probes have been evaluated by Biomedical Engineering and determined to be non-functional, unrepairable, and beyond economical repair. Without replacements, the service cannot maintain adequate imaging capacity to support patient care. 2.Scope of Work: This requirement needs to provide six (P/N: 9018) E14C4T Triplane endo transducers and six (P/N:UA2511) trays. 3.Place of Performance: The product is requested to be delivered to Surgery Service, building 100, MOR. 10,000 Bay Pines Blvd, Bay Pines, Florida 33744, via the Warehouse Building 36 for Equipment. 4.Period of Performance: The product is requested to be delivered no later than December 19th. 5.Type of Contract: Supply: Firm, Fixed Price. 6.Requirement Overview: The Contractor shall provide the full requested quantity of products listed below. 6.1 Salient Characteristics NAME BRAND - Equipment Requirement: GE Healthcare QTY. 6 - (P/N: 9018) E14C4T Triplane Endo Transducer QTY. 6 (P/N: UA2511) Reprocessing Trays for E14C4T Equipment Requirement: Minimum Required Features and Specifications Type / Intended Use: Must be a transrectal ultrasound transducer specifically designed for prostate imaging and biopsy guidance in urology applications. Must provide multi-plane (triplane) imaging capability allowing visualization of transverse, sagittal, and end-fire planes without changing probes. Frequency & Imaging Performance: Must operate within a frequency range of approximately 4 MHz to 14 MHz to provide both high-resolution and deep-penetration imaging of the prostate. Must support B-mode, M-mode, Color Doppler, and Power Doppler imaging modes (with optional elastography and contrast imaging if supported by the connected ultrasound system). Biopsy and Procedural Capability: Must include or support an integrated biopsy guide channel that allows both biplane and end-fire biopsy procedures without requiring probe exchange. Must accommodate standard 17- or 18-gauge biopsy needles through compatible biopsy guide attachments. Must permit real-time needle visualization during transrectal or transperineal prostate biopsy procedures. 4. Design & Ergonomics Must be a compact, endocavity-style probe suitable for patient comfort and operator ergonomics during transrectal use. title: High Consequence Infectious Disease (HCID) Staff Training
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE High Consequence Infectious Disease Staff Training Notice ID: 36C24827Q0097 Agency: Department of Veterans Affairs Sub-tier: Veterans Health Administration Contracting Office: NCO8 Notice Type: Sources Sought Proposed Set-Aside: To Be Determined NAICS Code: 611430 Product Service Code: U009 Response Deadline: 11/16/2026, 2:00 P.M. EST Place of Performance: Orlando VA Medical Center, 13800 Veterans Way, Orlando, Florida 32827 1. Purpose This Sources Sought Notice is issued solely for market research and acquisition-planning purposes. The Department of Veterans Affairs is seeking information from qualified business concerns capable of providing High Consequence Infectious Disease (HCID) training to staff of the Orlando VA Healthcare System. The information received may be used to determine the availability and capability of prospective contractors, the commercial availability of the required services, and the appropriate acquisition strategy, including whether a socioeconomic set-aside is supportable. Federal market research is used to determine whether capable sources and commercial services exist. For VA acquisitions, market research also supports the determination of whether capable certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses or Veteran-Owned Small Businesses are likely to submit offers at fair and reasonable prices. 2. Disclaimer This notice is not a solicitation. It is not a Request for Proposal, Request for Quotation, Invitation for Bid, or commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. Responses will not be considered offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Submission of information is voluntary, and the Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response. The Government is not obligated to provide respondents with the results of this market research. Respondents should not submit pricing proposals unless specifically requested below. Proprietary information should be clearly marked. The Government may use information received to refine its requirements and acquisition strategy. 3. Background The Orlando VA Healthcare System Emergency Management Service supports incident response and recovery operations involving natural and human-caused emergencies. Its mission includes coordination with Federal, State, local, Tribal, and territorial organizations during significant incidents and emergencies. The contemplated requirement would strengthen staff readiness to identify, manage, and respond safely to HCIDs while maintaining appropriate infection-prevention, occupational-safety, and patient-care practices. 4. Anticipated Scope The contractor would provide instructor-led virtual training and onsite practical training. The anticipated requirement includes the following components. 4.1 Virtual Interactive Training The contractor would conduct up to six virtual interactive classes, with no more than 50 participants per class, to train as many as 300 staff members. Anticipated subject areas include: HCID definitions, examples, epidemiology, and modes of transmission; Recognition, signs and symptoms, case definitions, and clinical presentation; Standard, contact, droplet, and airborne precautions; PPE selection and general donning and doffing procedures; Hand hygiene; Environmental cleaning and disinfection; Waste management; Patient isolation and transportation within the facility; Coordination with infection-prevention and public-health organizations; Safe specimen collection, packaging, and transportation; Post-exposure decontamination, reporting, prophylaxis, and monitoring; Occupational Health responsibilities; Risk communication, patient and family education, and reporting; Support for staff and patient emotional care; and Other related HCID preparedness topics identified by the Government. 4.2 Onsite Practical Training The contractor would conduct five onsite classes providing hands-on PPE donning and doffing instruction. Each class would contain no more than 15 participants, with practical training provided to a maximum of 60 staff members. The unused slots are designed to allow some flexibility to accommodate staffing schedles. Instruction would use a checklist-based method under which participants rotate between reading the procedure and demonstrating correct donning and doffing until competency is achieved. The Government anticipates providing the training PPE, including: 3M TR-600 powered air-purifying respirators; Tyvek 800 coveralls; Inner gloves; Extended-cuff outer gloves; Knee-high shoe covers; and Hospital scrubs. The contractor would also instruct participants on PPE-waste management and applicable post-exposure procedures. 4.3 Standards Training must be based on current authoritative guidance and comply with applicable requirements, including: Current Centers for Disease Control and Prevention guidance; OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard, 29 CFR 1910.1030; OSHA Personal Protective Equipment requirements, 29 CFR 1910.132; and OSHA Respiratory Protection Standard, 29 CFR 1910.134. 4.4 Schedule All courses are anticipated to be completed within 60 calendar days after contract award. Onsite training may occur outside normal business hours to accommodate staff schedules and may be scheduled over multiple consecutive days. Exact dates and times would be coordinated between the contractor and the designated VA point of contact. 5. Anticipated Contractor Responsibilities The contractor would be expected to: Provide qualified instructors with demonstrated HCID, infection-prevention, PPE, and adult-training experience. Conduct all virtual and onsite classes. Provide its own laptop and presentation equipment for onsite instruction because access to the VA computer network may not be available. Provide professionally prepared workbooks, handouts, manuals, and related instructional materials. Make virtual-training materials available electronically in PDF format. Maintain accurate attendance records. Provide completion certificates to participants. Assess each practical-training participant�s competency. Provide completed competency documentation to the participant and designated VA personnel. Administer participant feedback assessments at the end of each session. Summarize assessment results and provide the supporting feedback records to designated VA personnel. Monitor practical-training participants for signs of heat stress or other safety concerns while PPE is worn. Comply with applicable VA security, privacy, records-management, facility-access, and safety requirements. 6. Government-Furnished Support The Government anticipates: Coordinating mutually acceptable training dates and times; Providing suitable space for onsite classroom and practical instruction; Providing training PPE and related supplies; and Confirming that onsite participants are medically cleared before participating in PPE exercises. 7. Information Requested Interested organizations should submit a capability statement containing, at minimum: Business information Legal business name; Physical and mailing addresses; Website; Primary point of contact; Telephone number and email address; Unique Entity Identifier; Commercial and Government Entity code; and Current SAM.gov registration status. Business size and socioeconomic status Large or small business under the proposed NAICS code; Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business; Veteran-Owned Small Business; Women-Owned Small Business; Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business; 8(a) participant; HUBZone small business; or Other applicable socioeconomic category. PURPOSE: This Source Selection Plan (SSP) outlines the procedures that will be used to solicit architectural and engineering (AE) design services for Project 578-27-003 Renovate A Section on First Floor of Building 1. The goal of this project is to provide complete AE design services to renovate section A of the 1st floor of building 1. 2. This competitive procurement shall utilize a best value trade-off source selection process identified in FAR 15. 2.1.a: Source Selection Evaluation Board (SSEB): For the purpose of this acquisition, the SSEB will be same as the Technical Evaluation Board (TEB). 2.1.b: Below are the individual (TEB) evaluation criteria and ratings for the SF330s, listed in descending order of importance. FACTOR 1: SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE AND TECHNICAL COMPETENCE (30 Maximum Points) Subfactor 1A: Specialized Experience (15 Points). Subfactor 1B: Additional Experience (10 points). Subfactor 1C: Technical Competence (5 points). The A/E Firm shall demonstrate its specialized experience and technical competence in the design and construction period services for projects of similar size and complexity. Specialized project experience should include design of renovations to existing hospitals, renovations to buildings constructed prior to 1970 w/space constraints, design of Pathology Suites, and HVAC upgrades to existing hospitals. Additional experience includes mechanical, electrical, and structural engineering, architecture, interior design and finishes, physical security upgrades, building management systems/building automation systems (BMS/BAS), Computer-Aided Design and Drafting (CADD), critical path scheduling, fire protection, construction infection control protocols, design and installation of biological refrigeration and preservation systems, design and installation of vacuum tube transport systems, and project phasing and coordination in an active hospital setting. Recent is defined as services provided within the past seven (7) years with at least 50% of the Construction completed. Services & Deliverables provided under the contract/task order Period of Performance, including start and completion dates for design and construction if applicable. Estimated cost of construction based on AE s design Final construction cost (or projected final construction cost if still underway) The percentage of total cost resulting from changes due to AE omissions. The management approach The coordination of disciplines and subcontractors Quality control procedures Familiarity with VA Design Guides/Manuals, Master Specifications and other applicable standards. A resume for each of these key positions must be provided, corresponding with the title matching the disciplines listed for the project. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

description: Request for Information: Federal Occupational Health (FOH) National Staffing Support Services I. Introductory This is a Request for Information (RFI). This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this Request for Information is to obtain knowledge and information on potential vendor interest for project planning purposes. II. Project Description A. Background: FOH provides defined health services as well as consultation to Federal customer agencies exclusively through Interagency Agreements (IAAs). FOH is a leading provider of occupational health services (OHS) within the Federal Government, delivering services to numerous federal agencies and supporting a large federal workforce. Services are provided when FOH enters into agreements that are negotiated with federal departments and federal agencies� national headquarters, and/or with their regional/local components for products ranging from a standard package of OHS program components to an array of services, including clinical services delivery, expert medical consultation tailored to a particular federal agency�s OHS needs, wellness and health promotion, behavioral health services as well as organizational development related issues. FOH maintains sole responsibility for consulting with its federal customer partners. The Vendor�s main responsibility is to provide Contractors who deliver FOH services as outlined in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). FOH defines OHS as the seamless coordination of comprehensive services using a data-driven approach to assist agencies in achieving a culture of health and high performance. FOH comprehensive services include: Clinical Health Services (CHS) - Occupational medicine services, including urgent medical care, medical examination, employability consulting, and case review services that focus on assessing the medical ability of employees to perform their essential job duties safely, reducing lost workdays, and increasing employee productivity, as well as fitness for duty services that focus on the assessment of the ability of the employee to meet immediate job demands, increase employee productivity and improve employee performance. Environmental Health and Safety Services (EHSS) - Services to ensure a safe working environment through site assessments, environmental health oversight of all FOH occupied spaces, emergency preparedness and emergency response. Wellness and Health Promotion Services (WHPS) - Services to assist employees in achieving and maintaining good health so that they can sustain peak performance through fitness classes and wellness programs. Behavioral Health Services (BHS) � Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Work/Life and other behavioral health services designed to promote emotional well-being and a healthy life balance through stress management, financial legal counseling and professional referral. Operations and Management (O&M) � Services supporting FOH operations, management, and associated service areas. FOH services are designed to improve health outcomes and employee productivity, while reducing occupational health risks, absenteeism and overall employee health care costs. FOH�s mission is to be the occupational health provider of choice for the federal government.FOH staff plays a critical role in ensuring FOH maintains its status as the premier consultant provider of integrated OHS to federal agencies and their employees. By offering flexible, cost competitive solutions, FOH sets the standard for a culture of health and safety across the federal workforce. The Vendor is required to provide Contractor support for all occupational health services that FOH provides, including health promotion activities, data collection, and Agency/FOH initiatives requiring collaboration. Contractors are responsible for supporting FOH in the provision of occupational health services across the multiple services areas including but not limited to, account management, customer service, business operations, clinical health services, quality assurance, and case management. Contractors may also be responsible for supporting direct patient care, including providing safe, high-quality occupational health services, delivering health education, and raising awareness of key health indicators, associated risks to optimal health, and effective strategies for maintaining optimal health. FOH achieves these goals through services, including, but not limited to: a) Onsite clinical services b) Account management c) Financial analysis and cost estimation d) Billing and cost recovery e) Medical evaluations and clearances f) Quality analysis and review g) Complaint management h) Agreement management i) Specialized health services j) Consulting The quality of clinical services and strength of program effectiveness depend heavily on the expertise and experience of the Contractors. Contractors are expected to provide competent services to assist in the management of accounts and support client and organizational needs effectively. Contractors involved in providing specialized health services and medical case reviews must maintain the required credentials, licensure, and certifications appropriate to their role and per FOH�s requirements. Contractor participation in professional associations and pursuit of additional certifications and specialized training is strongly encouraged to keep current with identified best practices and medical advancements. Contractor promotion of such participation and pursuits is expected. Although required, pursuit of professional certifications, associations, and training is at the risk of Vendors. FOH will not be responsible for reimbursement. SPSs include FOH Occupational Health Centers, FOH Area Offices, and remote sites throughout the contract area. Services provided under this contract shall primarily be performed at the location identified in the Work Plan or otherwise specified by the COR (Attachment TBD). Purpose and Objectives: A. The primary purpose of this contract is to provide Contractor staffing services that do not involve direct care within Occupational Health Centers (OHCs). Direct care services within OHCs are considered secondary and are not guaranteed under this contract. To meet its mission, the scope of this contract shall cover FOH�s contract service requirements including, but not limited to, business operations, administrative, consultation, and delivery of occupational health support and direct services within the Continental United States (CONUS), and Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS). If within its Congressional authority, it is imperative that FOH acts quickly and maintains sufficient flexibility to meet the need, wherever the need arises. B. Project Requirements: Refer to the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS) C. Anticipated Period of Performance: The anticipated award date is June 30, 2027. The anticipated period of performance is five (5) years from award including a twelve (12) month base period with four (4) 12-month option periods. D. Capability Statement /Information Sought: Interested companies shall provide details of up to three (3) similar projects completed within the past three (3) years, including the following information: 1. Customer Name 2. Customer Point of Contact (POC) information/Client Email 3. Total Contract Value 4. Period of Performance 5. Brief Description of Services Provided 6. Is there a CPARS available, yes or no? E. Information Submission Instructions: Interested companies should: 1. Review all attachments included with this RFI notice 2. Submit a response that includes: o Feedback on the attachments (if any) o Complete answers to all questions in the attached "RFI Questions � Federal Occupational Health (FOH) National Staffing Support Services� document. o Complete answers to all items listed under "Capability Statement/Request for Information� Capability statements and responses shall be submitted via email to Ty

NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

This notice does NOT constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an announcement of an upcoming solicitation. � No contract will be awarded based on responses to this announcement. � The Government is under no obligation to issue a solicitation as a result of this notice. � The Government will not pay or reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting information in response to this announcement or any follow-up requests. � There is no solicitation package or bid documents available at this time; telephone inquiries requesting solicitation packages will not be honored. All information received will be held by NAVFAC Washington / FEAD Quantico to support acquisition strategy development and internal decision-making. I Background and Purpose: NAVFAC Washington / FEAD Quantico is conducting market research to determine the availability, capability, and capacity of qualified commercial contractors to provide complete basewide janitorial and custodial services across facilities located at Marine Corps Base (MCB) Quantico, Virginia. Current Acquisition Posture � This requirement is currently performed under an existing contract awarded through the Small Business Administration (SBA) 8(a) Business Development Program expiring on March 31, 2027. In accordance with the Small Business Act and federal acquisition regulations, the Government is primarily surveying the market to identify qualified and capable SBA-certified 8(a) small business concerns (including 8(a) single-entity, tribally-owned, ANC, or NHO participants) to assess whether a follow-on sole-source award or competitive 8(a) set-aside is the appropriate acquisition strategy. Secondarily, the Government invites capabilities statements from other SBA-certified socioeconomic small business categories (HUBZone, SDVOSB/VOSB, and WOSB/EDWOSB) to assess total small business industry capacity. II Summary Scope of Work: The Contractor shall provide all personnel, management, supervision, tools, equipment, transportation, materials, supplies, and quality control necessary to deliver comprehensive custodial and janitorial services at MCB Quantico facilities. Representative tasks include, but are not limited to: � Routine Cleaning & Sanitation: Daily cleaning, sanitizing, and restocking of restrooms, locker rooms, breakrooms, and common areas. � Surface Maintenance: Emptying trash, recycling receptacles, and bulk waste disposal. � Floor Care: Sweeping, dust-mopping, damp-mopping, buffing, and periodic stripping and waxing of hard surface floors. � Carpet Care: Routine vacuuming, spot cleaning, and periodic hot-water extraction deep cleaning. � Glass & Fixture Cleaning: Interior and exterior window cleaning, partition washing, and drinking fountain sanitization. � Security & Installation Access: Strict compliance with Department of the Navy and MCB Quantico physical security policies, including Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) credentialing for all personnel. Self-Performance Capacity: Confirmation of the firm�s ability to comply with FAR 52.219-14 (Limitations on Subcontracting), demonstrating that at least 50% of the cost of contract performance incurred for personnel will be expended on employees of the prime firm. 9. Installation Access & Clearance: Statement confirming capability to obtain DBIDS credentials and security vetting for on-site supervisory staff and cleaning personnel prior to contract commencement on April 1, 2027. 10. Staffing and Surge Capacity: Brief narrative explaining the firm�s methodology to recruit, train, and retain qualified custodial labor in the Quantico, VA area in compliance with the Service Contract Labor Standards (41 U.S.C. Chapter 67 / FAR 52.222-41). D. Relevant Past Performance 11. Provide up to three (3) relevant past performance projects completed within the last five (5) years that demonstrate experience similar in size, scope, and complexity to military basewide custodial operations: � Contract Number / Task Order Number (Note: If performed under an IDIQ or BPA, provide specific Task/Delivery Order details, not just the master contract). � Project Title, Facility Type, and Location. � Role (Prime Contractor or Subcontractor; include percentage of work self-performed). � Period of Performance (Award Date and Completion Date). � Total Contract Dollar Value and Approximate Square Footage Maintained. � Brief narrative description of the specific custodial services delivered. � Government or Commercial Point of Contact (Name, Agency/Company, Title, Phone Number, and Email). title: N4008527R0039 Design-Bid-Build (DBB) P-200, Aircraft Maintenance Hangar, Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Cherry Point, North Carolina
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. THERE WILL NOT BE A SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Mid-Atlantic is seeking eligible small business firms capable of performing construction services for Design-Bid-Build (DBB) P-200, Aircraft Maintenance Hangar, Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Cherry Point, North Carolina. This project constructs all operational and support facilities to support the basing of two F-35B Lightning II squadrons at the Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) in Cherry Point, North Carolina. New construction facilities include a low-rise, two-squadron module aircraft maintenance hangar, an aircraft parking apron, an aircraft ground/support training facility for the Center for Naval Aviation Technical Training (CNATT), a Ground Support Equipment (GSE) storage facility, an open steel-framed Operations Hazards Flammable Storage facility, and four Ready Service Magazines (RSMs). Demolition of existing facilities is required to clear the operational footprint, including the removal of Buildings 1667, 3978, 3986, 3996, 3997, 3998, 3999, and multiple hazardous waste storage shelters. The Aircraft Maintenance Hangar will be a low-rise, two-squadron module building containing high-bay space, crew and equipment space, and administrative space. The hangar will be constructed of concrete masonry units on a pile-supported reinforced concrete slab-on-grade foundation with structural steel framing, steel roof trusses, and a pre-finished insulated metal roof. Built-in equipment includes compressed air systems, personnel/freight elevators, 5-ton overhead bridge cranes, high-pressure cooling air systems, underwing and wet pipe fire suppression systems, raised access flooring, and backup generators. The Aircraft Ground/Support Training (CNATT) Facility will include administrative office spaces, five training classrooms, support spaces, and a small arms armory. The Ground Support Equipment (GSE) Storage Facility is a low-rise, high-bay single-story storage facility directly connected to the CNATT training facility. The Operations Hazards Flammable Storage Facility will be an open steel-framed structure featuring wire mesh partition separation by material type. The Ready Service Magazines (RSMs) consist of four masonry-constructed magazines (two per squadron) providing secure ammunition storage. The Aircraft Parking Apron includes new apron construction and renovation, equipped with electrical grounding, workstation kiosks, and sunshades. The project also includes extensive site preparation (clearing, excavation, grading, stormwater controls, and soil mitigation), paving and site improvements (covered aircraft wash racks, asphalt paving, sidewalks, dumpster pads, and landscaping), and comprehensive utility upgrades (electrical and communication distribution, water distribution, sanitary sewer, storm drainage, natural gas, oil-water separators, fire suppression foam containment, and industrial waste storage). All service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses (SDVOSB), veteran-owned small businesses (VOSB), certified HUB-Zone, certified 8(a), and women-owned small businesses (WOSB), and small businesses are encouraged to respond. Upon review of industry response to this Sources Sought Notice, the Government will determine whether a set-aside acquisition in lieu of full and open competition is in the Government�s best interest. The contract will include FAR clause 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting (DEVIATION 2021-O0008), which states that �It will not pay more than 85 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance, excluding the cost of materials, to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. Any work that a similarly situated entity further subcontracts will count towards the prime contractor�s 85 percent subcontract amount that cannot be exceeded.� It is requested that interested small businesses submit to the Contracting Officer a capabilities package, to include the Sources Sought Contractor Information Form and Sources Sought Project Information Form, provided as attachments to this notice. The Sources Sought Project Information Form and Sources Sought Project Matrix shall be used to document a minimum of two (2) up to a maximum of five (5) relevant construction projects for the offeror that best demonstrates experience on projects that are similar in size, scope and complexity as listed below. Projects submitted for the offeror shall be completed within the past fifteen (15) years from the date of issuance of this Sources Sought. For the purposes of this evaluation, a relevant project is further defined as: Size: A final construction cost of $35,000,000 or greater. Final construction cost is defined as the total price paid by the customer for the construction services, including original contract award amount and any modifications executed during performance. Scope: New construction or building addition/expansion of an aircraft maintenance hangar. Neither pre-engineered building systems nor renovation projects will be considered relevant. Complexity: For at least one relevant project (meeting the Size and Scope as defined above), the Offeror must demonstrate a column-free open hangar bay clear span not less than 200-ft. A project is defined as a construction project performed under a single task order or contract. For multiple award and indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity type contracts, the contract as a whole shall not be submitted as a project; rather Offerors shall submit the work performed under a task order as a project. Ensure that the project description clearly identifies whether the project is new construction or repair/renovation, addresses how the project meets the scope and complexity requirements as delineated above, and provides the final construction cost. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.
