title: INDUSTRY DAY - Richmond Army Reserve Center - MILCON
description: ***ADDRESS HAS BEEN UPDATED in the LOCATION/LOGISTICS SECTION*** The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Louisville District is issuing this special notice to announce an Industry Day for upcoming construction requirement for Construction of a 300-member Army Reserve Center (ARC) at Defense Supply Center, Richmond, VA. The Louisville District is considering Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) under 10 USC �2808a Other Transaction Authority for this requirement. This notice is for informational and planning purposes to allow interested parties to prepare for and provide feedback prior to the official Request for Qualifications (RFQ) release. INDUSTRY DAYS USACE intends to conduct an Industry Day on 19 November 2026 at 0900 Eastern Time to provide an overview of the project, potential acquisition strategy, and anticipated requirements. This event will provide interested parties with an opportunity to gain additional insight into the project and potential Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) approach under an Other Transaction (OT) framework, ask questions, and provide input in advance of the official RFQ release. General questions from industry participants will be permitted during the Industry Day; however, all discussions and responses provided during the event are considered unofficial and for informational purposes only. Statements made during the Industry Day do not constitute commitment, authorization, or binding guidance related to the future RFQ. Official Questions and Answers (Q&A) will be accepted and addressed following the release of the RFQ. Contractors and subcontractors interested in participating are requested to submit their Name, Company Name and contact information (email and phone) to the USACE Contracting Specialist no later than 1600 on 17 November 2026. Please use the information below to request Installation/Base access: Step 1: Badge Requests: To obtain pass/badge for one day or more, the contractor shall complete DBIDS pre-registration online using the following link DBIDS Pre-Enrollment or at https://dbids-global-enroll.dmdc.mil/preenrollui/#/landing-page. Once pre-registration has been complete, the visitor/contractor shall record and send the QR code/alpha-numeric code as a PDF/screenshot to the COR/PM via email (if multiple people are visiting or being vetted, the contractor shall compile all QR/alpha-numeric codes into a single email) at least 5 business days prior to visit/start date. The contractor shall include requested dates, times and names of personnel in the email. Failure to provide all the above information may lead to delays in requests being processed which could result in missed site visits, meetings etc. The COR/PM will notify the contractor upon their approval or denial. If approved, the contractor will have 30 days to pick up their visitor pass or project badge. When picking up the project badge the contractor is required to present their QR or alphanumeric code along with a valid form of ID. When filling out the QR code form, for the Service Site - select All. State � Virginia. Filter � Defense Logistics Agency Richmond. Note, a valid DOD ID card (Retired military, CAC etc.) is NOT permitted to be used to enter DCSR for commercial purposes. Step 2: Send a copy of their QR codes to Steven.Hall@DLA.MIL and he can forward them to security for vetting. Usually security will get back within a day or two of the submittal and let me know if they�ve been approved or not and then they are able to come and pick up a badge at the pass office. LOCATION/LOGISTICS Industry Day Presentation Location: 6090 Strathmore Road (Bldg 70), North Chesterfield, VA 23237 (Red, brick building with a large chimney right past the visitors center when you enter the gate) NOTE: Onsite parking space may be limited, overflow parking is available in the vicinity. PROJECT OVERVIEW Project Title: Construction of Army Reserve Center (ARC) Location: Richmond, Virginia Agency: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Louisville District NAICS Code: 236220 PROJECT DESCRIPTION Primary facilities include a 56,500 SF Army Reserve Center and 1200 SF Unheated Storage Building. Facilities will be designed in accordance with the Army Reserve Design Guide. Supporting facilities include land clearing, general site improvements, lighting, walks, signage, curbs and gutters, storm drainage, paving, information systems, and utility connections. Sustainability/Energy and cybersecurity measures are included. All fixtures, furnishings, and equipment will be provided. Antiterrorism force protection and physical security measures will be incorporated into the design including minimum standoff distances from roads, parking areas and vehicle unloading areas. Access for individuals with disabilities will be provided. Facilities will be designed to a minimum life of 40 years in accordance with DoD's Unified Facilities Criteria 1-200-02 including energy efficiencies, building envelope and integrated building systems performance. The project contains options such as: Bona fide need collateral equipment. The Contract Duration is estimated at 790 calendar days from Notice to Proceed on Construction Award. ACQUISITION STRATEGY � PRE-AWARD USACE, Louisville District plans to use a streamlined competitive selection process: Step 1 � White Papers/Qualification Statements: Interested parties will submit a Statement of Qualifications (max # of pages to be defined in formal RFQ. Following evaluation of the qualification packages, the Government intends to down-select a target of three (3) highest qualified firms to proceed to Step 2. Step 2 � Pitch Presentations: Down-selected firms will participate in live pitch meetings. One company will be selected as the Construction Manager for negotiation and award of Agreement 1 for preconstruction services. The Government intends to negotiate a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) for construction of the ARC, which will be added as a bilateral modification at a later date. ACQUISITION STRATEGY � AWARD The agreement would be awarded to the most qualified Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) to provide preconstruction services and construction. Phase 1 of the CMAR agreement would include pre-construction services. The selected CMAR would act as an expert consultant to the Government, collaborating directly with USACE and the third-party Designer of Record during active design progression. The Government�s intent is to award the Phase I Agreement for Preconstruction Services prior to the 95% design review meeting. Phase 2 of the agreement would include scope for all construction activities necessary to complete the project. The agreement will be Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP). All interested parties should monitor the official solicitation announcement, which will provide complete details and submission instructions. Draft documents may be provided at a future date for feedback and informational purposes only and are subject to change upon issuance of the formal Project RFQ. VIRTUAL PARTICIPATION OPPORTUNITY For those who are unable to attend the Industry Day event in person, the Louisville District plans to stream the event through Microsoft Teams. title: FCC Lompoc B&F Project 25Z6AXX Emergency Fire Escape Doors
description: STATEMENT OF WORK / REQUEST FOR QUOTE A. INTRODUCTION: 1. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP), FCC Lompoc, 3901 Klein Blvd., Lompoc, CA 93436, is seeking quotes from qualified vendors for the supply and delivery of nine (9) complete fire escape door assemblies, including doors, frames, and all required hardware. The doors are for a prison facility application and must meet all relevant local, state, and federal fire and life safety codes. 2. "Equal or Better" Product Substitution: Proposals must meet or exceed the specified product quality. If an alternative product or component is offered, the vendor must submit all technical documentation, certifications, and test results for consideration. 3. Government's Right of Final Technical Acceptance: The government retains the sole and final authority to determine technical acceptance for all submitted products, based on the provided documentation and compliance with stated standards. B. SCOPE OF WORK: 1. The vendor shall provide all materials as specified below. All components must be new, U.L. Listed or labeled by a recognized testing agency acceptable to the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) and conform to the standards referenced herein. C. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS: TABLE 1: COMPONENTS: All units shall be identical unless otherwise noted. Component Requirement Quantity 9 Complete Door Assemblies Door Size 36" wide x 80" high x 2" thick Door Material Hollow Metal Door, minimum 12 Gauge galvanneal steel Core Ribbed and Insulated (mineral core for fire rating is acceptable/preferred) Fire Rating Rating must be compatible with the wall's fire resistance rating, typically 75% of the wall's rating. See required fire rating for correctional facilities on Table 2 Handing 4 Left Hand Outswing, 5 Right Hand Outswing. Frame Material Minimum 12 Gauge galvanneal steel, fire-rated and labeled Frame Type Knock-down (KD) for drywall/unit masonry or welded for masonry. Frames are to be prepared for 80 series lock, keyed 2 sides strike, surface pull on both sides and prepped for PA closer. Finish Factory primed for field painting TABLE 2: FIRE RATING: The complete door assembly (door, frame, and all hardware) shall be 90 minutes fire rated. This rating must be compatible with the fire-resistance rating of the specific wall assembly in which the door will be installed, as dictated by the building's fire safety plan and local code requirements. Category Requirement Description Applicable Standards & Agencies Listing & Labeling All components must be listed and labeled by a recognized third-party testing agency acceptable to the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ). Underwriters Laboratories (UL), Intertek (WH), Factory Mutual (FM) Testing Standard Assemblies shall be tested under positive pressure conditions. NFPA 252, ANSI/UL 10C Labeling Visibility A permanent, legible fire rating label must be affixed to both the door and the frame and remain visible after installation for inspection purposes. N/A Code Compliance Vendor must confirm that all components, when installed as an assembly, comply with relevant building and safety codes for correctional facilities (Group I-3 Occupancies, IBC). NFPA 80 (Standard for Fire Doors and Other Opening Protectives) International Building Code (IBC) TABLE 3: HARDWARE SPECIFICATIONS: All hardware must be "listed" or "labeled" for use on a fire-rated assembly, compatible with the specified fire rating, and factory-prepped for ANSI/BHMA Grade 1 standards. Item Requirement Quantity per Door Notes Hinges Heavy-duty steel ball bearing hinges, UL Listed 3 Exit Device Panic Hardware/Fire Exit Hardware (rim or mortise type) self-latching 1 set Must be a crossbar or touch bar device, operable with an applied force of 15 lbs or less. Locking Must be openable from the egress side at all times without special knowledge or tools. Keyed access from the exterior is permitted. 1 set 80 series lock, keyed 2 sides strike, surface pull on both sides and prepped for PA closer. Door Closer Heavy-duty, adjustable, surface-mounted, UL Listed 1 unit Must be self-closing and ensure positive latching. Seals Smoke and draft control gasketing/seals 1 set Required for a complete smoke-rated assembly. Threshold [Specify if required, e.g., 1/2" beveled aluminum, non-combustible] 1 unit (if required) D. CODE AND STANDARD REQUIREMENTS: 1. All supplied materials and the complete assembly must comply with the latest editions of the following codes and standards (or local equivalents as adopted by the AHJ): NFPA 80: Standard for Fire Doors and Other Opening Protectives NFPA 101: Life Safety Code International Building Code (IBC) International Fire Code (IFC) OSHA requirements for exit routes UL 10C or NFPA 252: Standard for positive pressure fire testing of door assemblies UL 1784: Standard for Air Leakage Tests of Door Assemblies (if smoke rating is required) 2. Vendors must confirm that all components, when installed as an assembly, will bear a permanent, legible label from a recognized third-party testing agency (e.g., UL, Intertek/WH, FM). E. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: 1. Itemized pricing for doors, frames, hardware, and any included accessories. 2. Proposed lead time for manufacturing and delivery to FCC Lompoc 3. Confirmation of compliance with all referenced codes and standards. 4. Cut sheets/product data for all proposed items. F. DELIVERY OF MATERIALS: 1. Deliveries shipped directly to FCC LOMPOC can only be received between 7:30 a.m. and 2:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, excluding Federal Holidays. 2. POC: Mr. Fernando Pena, BOP Engineering Technician, FXPena@bop.gov, or 805-735-2771 3. FBOP will be responsible for receiving or signing deliveries. 4. title: Area of Interest: OSW Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation (CAPE) Modeling and Simulation
description: Amendment 1 - Answers to timely submitted questions are attached. NEW SUBMISSION DATE - Monday, November 16, 2026 - 4:00PM ET. ______________________________________________________________ The Department of War (DOW) Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation (CAPE) supports the Office of the Secretary of War (OSW). The Director of CAPE is the principal staff assistant to the Secretary of War for Cost Assessment & Program Evaluation. In fulfilling this role, the Director of CAPE provides independent, non-advocate, and data-driven analytical evaluations directly to the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of War regarding defense program investments, major force structure posture, and strategic resourcing trade-offs. The Director�s principal responsibilities include: Analyze and evaluate plans, programs, and budgets in relation to U.S. defense objectives, projected threats, allied contributions, estimated costs, and resource constraints. Review, analyze, and evaluate programs, including classified programs, for executing approved policies. Provide leadership in developing and promoting improved analytical tools and methods for analyzing national security planning and the allocation of resources. Ensure that the costs of DoW programs, including classified programs, are presented accurately and completely. Assess effects of DoW spending on the U.S. economy and evaluate alternative policies to ensure that DoW programs can be implemented efficiently. Currently, CAPE�s campaign- and mission-level Modeling and Simulation (M&S) relies on heavy, time-intensive physics engines (e.g., AFSIM) that execute discrete, bespoke combat runs. While highly detailed, these simulation approaches are too slow, computationally expensive, and inflexible to support executive-level sensitivity sweeps across multi-dimensional threat environments and Department warfighting capabilities. CAPE�s current environment leverages HPC resources that provide 1.5 terabytes (TB) of usable memory and 2,000 Central Processing Unit (CPU) cores with no wall clock time restraints. On average, individual simulation execution via AFSIM requires 1 hour of real time to complete and 20 gigabytes (GB) of accessible RAM. This constraint, coupled with sharp disparities in compute architecture, hardware availability, and security accreditation across existing CAPE enclaves restrict analysts to limited, manual workflows while preventing the execution of high-throughput, compute-intensive campaign analytics. CAPE is seeking innovative solutions to establish a next-generation modeling architecture, replacing its legacy M&S infrastructure. To dramatically compress the cycle time between defense budget queries and statistically defensible warfighting insights, the target environment must integrate three interdependent functional layers: (1) A high-performance simulation execution layer to execute large numbers of model (e.g., AFSIM) runs to span the parameter space. Runs in this layer are computationally intensive and resource demanding but will be executed infrequently and systematically using advanced Design of Experiments techniques. (2) A machine-learned surrogate emulation layer to train ultra-fast emulator models from simulation results and detect out-of-sample queries. While the government plans to develop and calibrate these surrogate emulators and analytical models in-house, the commercial solution must provide the extensible data staging, pipeline integration, and execution framework to ingest batch simulation results and host these government-developed models. (3) An intuitive self-service quantitative analysis layer housing pre-built methods for sensitivity analysis, marginal gain estimates, etc., and tools for custom analysis (e.g., tradespace decisions between range, speed, and lethality of weapon systems) and visualization. The solution must support both current operational needs and have flexibility to accommodate future growth in data volume, model complexity, user demand, and computational intensity. This next generation environment will establish an open, scalable, and unified computational backbone designed to modernize Department decision support. The scope of this effort includes the following core technical and performance requirements. A high-performance compute environment sized to meet demanding modeling, simulation, and analytic workloads. Proposed solution architectures should span options to allow for parameter evaluation in the simulation layer on the order of 1,200 individual simulations (i.e., light case - isolated missions only) to be executed within 10 hours real-time, up to 150,000 individual simulations (i.e., heavy case � full joint campaign) to be executed within 2 weeks real-time. Of note, current CAPE architecture would require 1 year of simulation execution runtime for the heavy case. Secure, efficient, data and software movement both into and out of the environment, as well as the ability to interface with external networks to enable transfer of data in accordance with applicable security and access controls. The environment must support network throughput of 100 Mbps - 1 Gbps. The solution must also support connectivity over HTTPS to designated external OSW and mission-relevant data sources, including OSW CAPE-furnished databases and other authorized repositories (e.g., War Data Platform), as applicable. Ability to accommodate evolving development ecosystems and diverse sets of software including M&S tools and analytic technologies. This includes modern software (e.g., Python, R, Java, etc.), scalable data platforms, scalable parallelizable processes (e.g., containers), optimization tools (e.g., GAMS), artificial intelligence capabilities (e.g., large language models), and neural network development (e.g., PyTorch), provided they can be incorporated in a secure and maintainable manner. The solution must enable efficient onboarding, integration, and removal of models and software as mission needs evolve. The Government will retain full operational tenant administration, maintaining exclusive control over user access provisioning, role-based security permissions, data ingestion, proprietary model uploads, container orchestration, and analytical query execution. The Commercial provider will be responsible for turnkey, managed platform and infrastructure IT operations, including hardware availability, operating system patching, network performance, automated system backups, and baseline cybersecurity hardening, ensuring government analysts and technical leads are fully insulated from day-to-day hardware maintenance and IT administration.

title: Germany – Public road transport services – Vergabe von Personenbeförderungsleistungen im Linienverkehr mit Kraftfahrzeugen im Landkreis Böblingen, Verkehrsraum Linienbündel 2 "Strudelbach"
description: Der öffentliche Auftraggeber ist zuständiger Aufgabenträger im öffentlichen Personennahverkehr (ÖPNV) nach § 8 Abs. 3 Satz 1 PBefG i. V. m. § 6 Abs. 1 des Gesetzes über die Planung, Organisation und Gestaltung des öffentlichen Personennahverkehrs Baden-Württemberg (ÖPNVG BW). Der Auftraggeber ist gem. § 6 Abs. 3 ÖPNVG BW damit auch zuständige Behörde im Sinne der EU-Verordnung (EG) Nr. 1370/2007 (VO 1370/2007). Der Landkreis ist damit für die Sicherstellung eines ausreichenden Verkehrsangebots in seinem Wirkungskreis zuständig (§ 8 Abs. 3 PBefG). Nachdem die aktuelle Verkehrsbedienung im Linienbündel BB02 zum 30.06.2027 endet, war die Verkehrsleistung ab dem 01.07.2027 zu gewährleisten, mithin neu auszuschreiben. Zur Vergabe kommen die Busverkehrsleistungen auf den nachfolgenden aufgelisteten VVS-Linien: – Linie 634 Weissach - Flacht - Rutesheim - Leonberg – Linie 634A Weissach - Flacht - Perouse - Rutesheim (Schülerverkehr) – Linie N62 Leonberg - Gebersheim - Rutesheim - Perouse - Flacht - Weissach und zurück Es handelt sich ausschließlich um Linienverkehre die nach § 42 PBefG genehmigt werden sollen. Der Auftragnehmer hat den vorgegebenen Fahrplan zu erfüllen; dieser ist in Anhang LB.1 beigefügt. In Anhang LB.2 und Anhang LB.3 finden sich die zugehörigen Planungshilfen. Im Rahmen der Inbetriebnahme des Eisenbahninfrastrukturprojektes Stuttgart 21 (S21) kann es zu Verschiebungen im S-Bahn- und/ oder Regionalverkehr kommen. Die Deutsche Bahn hat im Juni 2026 eine stufenweise Inbetriebnahme ab vrsl. Dezember 2031 angekündigt. Daher sind die vorgegebenen Busfahrpläne nach Umstellung der S-Bahn- und/oder Regionalverkehre durch den Auftragnehmer auf Kompatibilität mit den dann geltenden S-Bahn- und/ oder Regionalverkehrsfahrplänen zu überprüfen. Mögliche Anpassungen sind mit dem Aufgabenträger und ggf. dem VVS rechtzeitig abzustimmen und umzusetzen. Das Letztentscheidungsrecht hat der Aufgabenträger. Der Auftraggeber stellt klar, dass es sich bei dem beschriebenen Mechanismus um Optionen im Sinne des § 132 Abs. 2 S. 1 Nr. 1 GWB handelt, welche im Falle einer, auch späteren, Inbetriebnahme von S 21 eine Auftragsänderung ohne Neuausschreibung ermöglichen. Die Auftragsvergabe fällt in den Anwendungsbereich der Richtlinie 2009/33/EG des Europäischen Parlaments und des Rates (Richtlinie zur Förderung sauberer Fahrzeuge — CVD). Näheres ist Ziff. 5.1. zu entnehmen.

description: Naantalin kaupungin yksiköt (Tilaaja) pyytää tarjouksia rakennusurakointitöiden toteuttamisesta sopimuskaudelle. Hankinnan kohteena olevat työt toteutetaan joko erikseen minikilpailutettavina toimeksiantoina tai suoraan hankittavina töinä sopimusehtojen mukaisesti. Rakennusurakoita kilpailutetaan lisäksi kohdekohtaisilla urakkakilpailulla. Sopimuskauden arvioitu alkamisajankohta on 1.1.2027. Lisäksi Tilaaja varaa mahdollisuuden kahteen optiovuoteen (1+1). title: Finland – Financial and insurance services – Hankintailmoitus: LapIT Oy:n vakuutusturvan hankinnan kilpailutus
description: LapIT Oy (myöhemmin Tilaaja) pyytää tarjouksia vakuutusturvasta ja siihen liittyvistä palveluista tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. LapIT Oy:n vakuutusturva ja sen laajuus on kuvattu tarjouspyynnön liitteissä. Ensimmäinen vakuutuskausi on 1.1.2027-31.12.2027. Tämän jälkeen vakuutuskausi on kalenterivuosi. Tarjous jätetään alkaen täydestä kalenterivuodesta (2027). LapIT Oy:llä on oikeus vakuutuskausien aikana kilpailuttaa vakuutukset uudelleen ja siirtää vakuutukset kilpailutuksen voittajalle. Vakuutukset ovat voimassa toistaiseksi voimassa olevana. Hankinnan sopimuskausi on kolme (3) vuotta, jonka jälkeen LapIT Oy:llä on oikeus jatkaa sopimuskautta yhdellä (1) kahden (2) vuoden optiokaudella. Optiokauden jälkeen LapIT Oy:llä on oikeus jatkaa hankintaa toistaiseksi voimassa olevana optiokautena. Lisähankintamahdollisuus: LapIT Oy varaa oikeuden laajentaa sopimusta, mikäli se perustuu hankintamenettelyn aikana tiedossa olleisiin ja hankinta-asiakirjoissa mainittuihin sopimusehtoihin tai niiden muuttamista koskeviin ehtoihin, niiden rahallisesta arvosta riippumatta, ja nämä ehdot ovat selkeät, täsmälliset ja yksiselitteiset, eivätkä ne muuta hankintasopimuksen yleistä luonnetta (1397/2016, 14 luku, 136 §, 2 mom., 1 kohta); tai mikäli alkuperäisen sopimuskumppanin on tarpeen suorittaa lisätöitä tai -palveluja taikka ylimääräisiä tavarantoimituksia, jotka eivät sisältyneet alkuperäiseen sopimukseen, ja jos sopimuskumppanin vaihtaminen ei ole mahdollista taloudellisista tai teknisistä syistä ja aiheuttaisi merkittävää haittaa tai kustannusten merkittävää päällekkäisyyttä hankintayksikölle (1397/2016, 14 luku, 136 §, 2 mom., 2 kohta). LapIT Oy on pohjoissuomalainen ICT -infra ja perustietotekniikan palveluita omistajilleen tuottava in-house -yhtiö. Omistajiimme kuuluu pohjoisen Suomen kuntia, hyvinvointialueita, kunta- ja hyvinvointialueyhtymiä sekä kuntaomisteisia osakeyhtiötä. LapIT Oy on velvollinen kilpailuttamaan tarvitsemansa palvelut markkinoilta hankintalain mukaisesti. Hankinnan kilpailutus on hankintalain (Laki julkisista hankinnoista ja käyttöoikeussopimuksista 1397/2016) mukainen EU-kynnysarvon ylittävä palveluhankinta. Hankinnan kilpailutuksen sisältö vakuutusturvan osalta on seuraavanlainen: Työtapaturma- ja ammattitautivakuutus: - Lakisääteinen ryhmätapaturmavakuutus työntekijöille (TyTAL) Henkilövakuutukset: - Sairauskuluvakuutukset (sairauskuluvakuutus, ryhmävakuutus) Muut tarkemmat tiedot on ilmoitettu muualla hankintailmoituksessa, tarjouspyynnössä sekä hankinta-asiakirjoissa ja liitteissä.

title: Bulgaria – Repair and maintenance services of checking apparatus – „Изпълнение на дейности, свързани с пожарогасителни и пожароизвестителни системи на МВнР, с две обособени позиции“
description: Предметът на обществената поръчка е: „Изпълнение на дейности, свързани с пожарогасителни и пожароизвестителни системи на МВнР, с две обособени позиции“, както следва: Обособена позиция № 1: „Абонаментно обслужване на 2 бр. пожарогасителни системи, обхващащи помещение „сървър“ в подземното етажно ниво и помещение „архив ценни книжа“ на 7 етажно ниво в Централното управление на МВнР“. Предметът на обособената позиция включва ежемесечно абонаментно сервизно обслужване: планово-профилактични прегледи, техническа поддръжка и при необходимост – ремонт, на 2 бр. пожарогасителни системи, обхващащи помещение „сървър“ в подземното етажно ниво и помещение „архив ценни книжа“ на 7 етажно ниво в Централното управление на МВнР, с газообразно вещество FM-200 в МВнР, производство на ЕЛ ПИ ДЖИ С.А., Испания, за срок от 24 месеца. Обособена позиция № 2: „Абонаментно сервизно следгаранционно поддържане на пожароизвестителни системи „ZETFAS 3000”, „Унипос 7000“ и „Унипос 4000“, монтирани в обекти на МВнР“. Предметът на обособената позиция включва ежемесечно абонаментно сервизно обслужване: планово-профилактични прегледи, техническа поддръжка и при необходимост – ремонт, на пожароизвестителни системи „ZETFAS 3000”, „Унипос 7000“ и „Унипос 4000“, монтирани в обекти на МВнР, за срок от 12 месеца. Система „ZETFAS 3000” ще се поддържа до монтиране на нова пожароизвестителна система в ЦУ на МВнР. Система „ZETFAS 3000” се предава за обслужване в текущото си състояние. След отпадане на обслужването на „ZETFAS 3000”, при месечно обслужване ще се изплаща само стойността на обслужването на системи „Унипос 7000“ и „Унипос 4000“. Естеството и обемът на дейностите, предметът на възлагане, както и изискванията за изпълнение на поръчката, са подробно представени в Техническите спецификации за Обособени позиции № 1 и № 2, представляващи Приложение № 1 към настоящата документация. Условията, при които ще се реализира предметът на поръчката, правата и задълженията на страните, са подробно разписани в Проектите на договор за възлагане на обществената поръчка по Обособени позиции № 1 и № 2, представляващи Приложение № 2 към настоящата документация.
